Setting: k >= 2 pairwise distinct real members. Each is a cubic f = 2t+1 + t(t+1)(a t + c) with a != 0 (any sign), or the member 2t+1, which can occur at most once. Assume f_j - 1 | F - 1 and f_j + 1 | F + 1, where F = prod f_j. Notation: Q = (a, c), O = (0,0) for 2t+1, V = 1/a, u = c/a, R = -2V - u(1-u)/2, w (resp. v) the upper root of g = (f-1)/t (resp. h = (f+1)/(t+1)), alpha = |2w+1|^2 - 1 = (8 + 2c - 2a)/a, beta = |2v+1|^2 - 1 = (8 - 2c)/a.

STEP 0 (cited). By the sign-free Lemma 6 (equal real-root multisets of f_j -+ 1) and the sign-free Lemma 3, every cubic member lies in D = {a > 0, c^2 < 8a, (a-c)^2 < 8a}, because the discriminants are (a-c)^2 - 8a and c^2 - 8a. If g_j had a real root, all f_l - 1 would be a_l G for one common G, which Lemma 3 excludes; with 2t+1 present the multiset {0} forbids it. Distinct members share no non-real special point: g(-1) = 2 and h(0) = 2 force g_l = g_i. Hence f_l(w_i) != 1 and f_l(v_i) != -1 for l != i.

C1 (PROVED, any signs).
- Congruences: f_l - 1 = 2(1-rho)t + (c_l - rho c_i)t(t+1) mod g_i and f_l + 1 = 2(1-rho)(t+1) + (c_l - rho c_i)t(t+1) mod h_i, with rho = a_l/a_i. Valid for all real a_i != 0 and all (a_l, c_l).
- Half-trace over the roots of g_i: htr(f_l - 1) = a_l<n^w_i, P_l - P_i> = <m^w_i, Q_l - Q_i>. Over the roots of h_i: htr(-f_l - 1) = -a_l<n^v_i, P_l - P_i> = <m^v_i, Q_l - Q_i>. Here n^w = (-u-1, R), n^v = (2-u, R), so n^v - n^w = (3,0) (Re(v+1) - Re w = 3/2). In the (a,c)-chart, m^w + m^v = (3/a_i, 0), and 2t+1 is the point O.
- If disc g_i < 0 (resp. disc h_i < 0), which forces a_i > 0, the half-trace equals Re f_l(w_i) - 1 (resp. Re(-f_l(v_i)) - 1).
- Moduli, relative chart: put lam = 1 - a_l/a_i and kap = c_l - (a_l/a_i)c_i. Then |f_l(w_i)|^2 - 1 = 2(-lam(1+u) + kap R) + (u + 2V)(4lam^2 + 2lam kap(1-u) + 2kap^2 V) and |f_l(v_i)|^2 - 1 = 2(-lam(2-u) - kap R) + (1 - u + 2V)(4lam^2 - 2lam kap u + 2kap^2 V). Both forms are positive definite on D. For O, (lam, kap) = (1, 0).

C2 (PROVED, every k >= 2, cubic members only, collinear Q_l).
- Choose the endpoint i: on a non-vertical line, the unique member with minimal a; on a vertical line, either endpoint. Let e = Q_j - Q_i, with j the other endpoint. Then Q_l = Q_i + s_l e with s_l in (0,1] and e_a >= 0.
- By C1, the Re-excesses at w_i and v_i are s_l<m^w_i, e> and s_l<m^v_i, e>, whose sum is 3 s_l e_a/a_i >= 0.
- Take z = w_i if <m^w_i, e> >= 0, otherwise z = v_i. Every other factor (f_l(w_i), resp. -f_l(v_i)) then has Re >= 1 and is != 1 by Step 0, so its modulus is > 1.

- Only the modulus equations at one member are used, so the result holds for the modulus-only system.

C3 (PROVED, every k >= 2, all u_i = u0, with or without 2t+1).
- Ray identity: for every member Q_l = (a_l, u0 a_l), including O, f_l(w_i) = 1 + 2 d w_i with d = 1 - a_l/a_i. Then |.|^2 - 1 = -2d(1+u0) + 4d^2(u0 + 2V_i), and |w_i|^2 = u0 + 2V_i > 0.
- u0 <= -1: take i = argmax a; then d is in (0,1] for all others, so every modulus is > 1.
- u0 > -1 without 2t+1: take i = argmin a; then d < 0, so every modulus is > 1.
- u0 > -1 with 2t+1 and one cubic: F(w) = 2w + 1 != 1.
- u0 > -1 with 2t+1 and >= 2 cubics: let i = argmin a and j = argmax a.
  - If alpha_i >= 0, at w_i the cubic factors are > 1 and the linear factor is >= 1.
  - Otherwise alpha_j < alpha_i < 0, since V_j < V_i at the same u0. By strict convexity in d with d in (0,1], every factor at w_j has modulus < 1.
- Every case contradicts prod = 1. Members odd in t + 1/2 are the case u0 = 1/2.
